summary: a SIGTERM to every process of a case during its wait, its keepers among them, ends them all, and the scenario sees its service ended by the stop

argv: exec ${CC:-cc} -std=c99 -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=0 -DRACH2_HOSTTEST -O1 -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -I tests/host -I tools/etude/include -I tools/etude -I tools/etude/posix -I tools/etude/guest -I utils tests/host/etude_scenario_hosttest.c tools/etude/posix/scenario.c tools/etude/posix/case_main.c tools/etude/serial.c tools/etude/processor.c tools/etude/posix/qemu.c tools/etude/qemu_profile.c tools/etude/posix/exec.c ${SRC}/tools/etude/posix/keeper.c tools/etude/posix/process.c tools/etude/posix/store.c tools/etude/capture.c tools/etude/history_json.c tools/etude/guest/guest.c tools/etude/guest/fixture.c tools/etude/guest/wire.c utils/sha256.c -o ${WORK}/test

faults.name: controller-handlers
faults.summary: the keeper keeps its controller's handlers, so the scenario's SIGTERM handler writes a byte into the keeper's event pipe

lines: stop-all: the attempt did not end within

faults.name: term-kills-keeper
faults.summary: the keeper takes SIGTERM's default and dies before it reports its service's end

lines: stop-all: the service's end by the stop was seen
